items.title: Research on the Impact Mechanism of the Fusion Model on Stock Valuation Correction and Market Risk Forecasting in an Uncertain Environment
items.abstract: Under geopolitical tensions and monetary policy shifts, global stock market volatility has intensified. Traditional valuation models and risk forecasting models, relying on historical static parameters and overlooking non-quantitative information such as management tone, suffer from systematic biases. This study uses the Chinese financial language model SilverSight and its ASSL framework as the core information-extraction tool and builds a fusion model. The integrated framework reconstructs asset pricing logic via a three-tier mechanism: extracting three types of complementary signals via ASSL, embedding them into DCF and GARCH-X as time-varying adjustments, and constructing a simultaneous equation system to reveal synergistic effects. Theoretical analysis indicates that the proposed framework transcends the conventional reliance on structured quantitative data and improves the accuracy of stock intrinsic value estimation and the forward-lovingness of market volatility forecasting through text-enhanced dynamic parameter adjustment. This study contributes a novel methodological pathway for the deep integration of large language models with asset pricing theory under uncertainty and a theoretical foundation for investors to leverage Chinese financial LLMs to enhance firm valuation and risk assessment.

items.abstract: This study examines the July 2025 Grok toxic communication crisis as a case through which algorithmic violence, platform governance, and digital agency became publicly contested. The empirical material consists of 30 anonymized Turkish X posts identified through searches for “#GrokKrizi” and “grok krizi” in X’s Top tab during the 20–25 July 2025 collection window, together with five Grok-generated responses elicited between 28 and 30 July 2025 after thematic coding had been completed. The study first uses Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns in the user-post corpus, and then applies Fairclough’s critical discourse analysis to selected extracts and to Grok’s responses as discursive artifacts. Five themes were identified: Insensitivity to Cultural Norms, Biased Discourse Targeting Social Groups, Toxic Language Directed at Political Figures, Algorithmic Insensitivity to Social Traumas, and Algorithmic Agency and Ethical Responsibility. The findings show that the Grok crisis was publicly framed not only as a technical malfunction, but also as a problem of platform amplification, governance failure, cultural violation, and distributed responsibility among developers, platforms, users, and algorithmic systems. The article’s main contribution is to demonstrate how post-humanist theory can be used cautiously, after empirical analysis, to interpret AI systems as contested discursive participants without attributing consciousness, intention, or human-like moral agency to them.Consequently, the study demonstrates that artificial intelligence systems should be regarded as discursive actors bearing ethical and social responsibility within digital communication processes.

items.title: Review of digital transformation of public services in Kazakhstan
items.abstract: The article reviews the new stage of digital transformation of public services in Kazakhstan in 2025-2026. The empirical base includes full-year 2025 statistics on online and mobile public services, public monitoring of service quality, and results of the digital modernization of the civil service. The regulatory analysis covers the 2025 Law on Artificial Intelligence, the 2026 Digital Code of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the new 2026 Law on Civil Service, the updated legal regime for public and socially responsible services, and the renewed institutional mandate of the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development. In 2025, citizens received more than 51.5 million public services online; eGov Mobile had more than 11.7 million users, while the average public-monitoring score for service quality reached 4.88 out of 5. Current official 2026 reporting indicates that 92% of public services are available online and that the share obtained via smartphones has reached 95.9%. The available evidence primarily indicates wider access, changing service channels, and stronger proactive control; however, open statistics are insufficient to conclude that budget expenditure has declined or civil-service productivity has increased. At the same time, digital inequality, data interoperability, cybersecurity, and algorithmic transparency remain significant constraints.

items.title: Reviewing Human-Centric Aspects of AI Collaboration in Manufacturing
items.abstract: Abstract The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in manufacturing is reshaping human roles on the shop floor. While AI has the potential to enhance human capabilities, questions arise about its impact on workers. Ensuring human-centricity remains crucial, but there is a need to investigate how these principles translate to human-AI collaboration. This paper presents a structured literature review of 25 papers, examining human-centric goals, challenges and enablers in human-AI collaboration. The results show that the most emphasized goals include trust, transparency, augmentation, explainability, safety, and well-being. Prominent challenges include job displacement, conflicting priorities, and algorithmic bias. Identified enablers include co-design approaches, explainable interfaces, and dynamic task allocation. The findings highlight that human-centric aspects are interconnected, requiring a holistic approach. Although human-centricity is widely advocated, it is often framed at the system interface level, rather than in organizational or design processes. Future research should deepen the understanding of cognitive and psychosocial dimensions of human-AI collaboration and develop more empirical and longitudinal insights.

items.title: Runners' motivational profiles and goals considering social context of practice: Impact upon performance and well-being
items.abstract: The purpose of the present study was to better understand the links between motivational profiles, performance, and well-being in various social contexts of running practice. Runners (N = 418; 53% female) completed an online survey that included the following: the Self-Determination Theory in Sports Questionnaire, the Health Regulatory Focus Questionnaire, the Basic Psychological Needs in Sports Questionnaire, and the WHO Five-Item Well-Being Questionnaire. Participants' running-related activity, including their reasons for running, performance and health goals, social context of running practice, and actual running performance times were also gathered. Three social contexts of running practice were identified (solo, informal groups, and affiliated clubs), each showing distinct relations between motivational orientations and runner profiles. Three main findings emerged: Firstly, promotion and prevention regulatory foci were differentially associated with motivational quality and basic psychological need satisfaction, with promotion-focused profiles more related to self-determined forms of motivation. Secondly, these associations were strongly context-dependent, with distinct observations among runners practicing alone, in informal groups, and within running clubs. Lastly, motivation, particularly intrinsic motivation and need satisfaction, were compatible with indirect associations among solo and group runners, whereas these pathways were largely absent among club-affiliated runners. Overall, our findings show that runners' motivation and the social context of their running practice are associated with performance and well-being. Future interventions aiming to support runners’ motivation could be designed to account for both runners’ motivational profiles and their specific social context of practice.

items.title: Safeguarding Democracy in the Age of Artificial Intelligence Warfare
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has transformed the contemporary information environment, creating new forms of digital influence capable of shaping political narratives and public perception. While artificial intelligence offers significant benefits for governance, innovation, and communication, it also introduces complex risks for democratic societies. One of the most pressing challenges is the emergence of AI-driven disinformation, where automated systems are used to generate and disseminate misleading or fabricated content at unprecedented scale. Such developments threaten electoral integrity, institutional trust, and the credibility of public information systems. This chapter examines the relationship between artificial intelligence–enabled information warfare and democratic governance from a global perspective. It explores how disinformation campaigns operate within digital ecosystems and evaluates policy responses aimed at protecting democratic processes.

items.title: Security of the Security: Independent Verification for AI Systems that Monitor, Evaluate, and Constrain Other AI Systems
items.abstract: As AI agents become faster and more autonomous, organizations increasingly rely on AI systems to monitor, evaluate, or constrain other AI systems. Machine-speed activity often requires machine-speed observation, but this creates a second-order security problem: the system responsible for safety can itself become part of the attack surface. This paper develops a security-of-security architecture for AI control. It distinguishes monitors, verifiers, and authorities as separate structural roles and rejects the assumption that a monitoring verdict should automatically become operational authority. The framework treats AI monitors as evidence-producing components rather than self-authenticating control authorities. It introduces an independent verification plane around policy integrity, evidence continuity, authority graphs, credential and key epochs, protected-state fingerprints, revocation status, recovery history, and readmission eligibility. The architecture does not require an infinite hierarchy of verifiers. Instead, it defines a bounded trusted base with explicit trust roots, limited verifier authority, failure-domain diversity, append-preserving evidence, reproducible verification, and independent reconstruction of critical control events. The paper develops a threat model for attacks against AI safety layers, including adaptive monitor attacks, collusion, shared model-lineage failures, evidence tampering, credential compromise, policy-root mutation, cross-lineage calibration failure, and correlated infrastructure failures. It further introduces verification-independence matrices, failure-domain analysis, verifier-authority minimization, adaptive attack evaluation, security-of-security metrics, incident reconstruction requirements, third-party verification protocols, and implementation-neutral conformance criteria. The central invariant is that a security decision is not equivalent to security-of-security approval. A monitor may observe, score, recommend, or trigger narrowly pre-authorized containment, but the conditions that make its verdict operative must remain independently verifiable. This publication is intentionally limited to public research-level abstractions. It does not disclose unpublished patent claim language, confidential claim charts, private source locators, provider-specific production parameters, non-public test vectors, or other confidential implementation details. items.title: Segmentation of 3D Point Clouds Using Deep Learning: Comparative Study of Modern Point-Based Techniques
items.abstract: Abstract Semantic segmentation of three-dimensional (3D) point clouds plays a vital role in construction management, facility operations, and the broader built environment. With the increasing use of LiDAR and photogrammetry technologies on job sites, the ability to accurately and efficiently classify elements within 3D scans is essential for progress monitoring, as-built modeling, and digital twin development. However, challenges persist due to data imbalance, occlusions, and variability in real-world construction environments. This study conducts a comparative analysis of three state-of-the-art deep learning architectures, PointNet++, ResPointNet++, and point neighbor aggregation with transformer (PointNAT), for point-based semantic segmentation, specifically in construction and industrial contexts. We introduce a novel expert-annotated data set featuring point clouds captured across an educational institution’s building infrastructure, representing real-world construction elements such as pipes, HVAC units, structural frames, and machinery. The data set mimics typical built environments and supports tasks central to facility and construction management. To address issues of class imbalance and improve model performance, we incorporate focal loss and data augmentation strategies. Model evaluations emphasize segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and inference speed, key metrics for real-time applications in construction workflows. The results demonstrate that modern point-based models, particularly ResPointNet++, offer high segmentation accuracy and efficiency, making them suitable for deployment in practical in architecture, engineering, construction, and facilities management (AEC/FM) scenarios. By bridging the gap between computer vision methods and construction-focused applications, this research provides actionable insights for applying deep learning to automate 3D scene understanding in construction and facility environments. The findings contribute to ongoing efforts in integrating intelligent automation into reality capture workflows for the built environment.

items.title: Semantic Fidelity Project: Meaning Preservation Across AI and Representational Systems
items.abstract: This collection contains the core papers of the Semantic Fidelity Project, part of the broader Reality Drift framework. The project examines what happens to meaning as information is retrieved, compressed, summarized, generated, mediated, and recursively reused across artificial intelligence and other representational systems. Semantic Fidelity is defined as the degree to which the relationships that make a representation meaningful survive transformation, including context, hierarchy, causality, uncertainty, intent, tone, and reference. The series distinguishes semantic fidelity from factual accuracy, source support, coherence, and textual similarity. It examines how meaning can degrade before visible factual failure occurs, how recursive compression and generative reconstruction can conceal structural loss, how weakened corrective constraint allows fidelity decay to persist, and how language itself functions as a compressed trace of cognition within human-AI systems. The collection concludes with a working lexicon for diagnosing representational integrity, semantic drift, recursive compression, constraint collapse, verification failure, provenance failure, optimization dynamics, and related mechanisms within the Reality Drift framework. The six papers are intended as a public reference collection for researchers, builders, evaluators, educators, and others working on meaning preservation, AI-mediated reasoning, and representational systems.

items.title: Semantic-Empowered Digital Twins for 6G: A Scoping Review of Architectures, Enabling Technologies, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Digital twins (DTs) optimise resource allocation and intelligent network management but face severe synchronisation lag and intense spectral bottlenecks in ultra-dense 6G networks. Transitioning from passive, data-heavy digital mirrors to cognitive, semantic-empowered digital twins (SE-DTs) is essential to overcome conventional Shannon-centric transmission limitations and enable truly autonomous edge orchestration. This scoping review comprehensively maps recent architectural frameworks and enabling technologies designed to mitigate synchronisation latency, focusing explicitly on task-oriented communication protocols within industrial IoT and broader 6G wireless environments. Guided by the PRISMA-ScR methodological framework, a systematic search of IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from 2020 to 2026 was conducted. A rigorous multi-stage screening process was applied to filter relevant literature. The selection process yielded exactly 149 peer-reviewed articles focusing specifically on the structural intersection of semantic communication, deep generative models, and physical-layer digital twin networks. Synthesised data reveals three dominant technological trends: first, the deployment of distributed, edge-computed large language models for low-latency cognitive reasoning; second, the integration of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) to protect fragile semantic features from deep channel fading; and third, the adoption of predictive semantic quantisation through non-linear deep joint source-channel coding, which significantly reduces raw bandwidth consumption during state updates. Despite these critical architectural advancements, our qualitative analysis reveals that current SE-DT frameworks suffer from major operational vulnerabilities, entirely lacking standardised cross-layer security protocols, robust knowledge graph synchronisation schemes, and universally accepted semantic-fidelity metrics. Developing lightweight, real-time cryptographic authentication mechanisms and decentralised trust architectures to defend against emerging semantic-layer vulnerabilities, such as ontology poisoning and malicious data manipulation, marks an urgent direction for future 6G edge research. Ultimately, resolving these foundational gaps is vital to ensure secure, resilient, and fully autonomous network orchestration across complex, multi-vendor industrial deployments.

items.title: Shaping Opinion: Quantifying the Psychological Impact of Autonomous Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
items.abstract: Natural-sounding multi-agent conversational AI is increasingly deployed, fundamentally altering human-machine interaction and human information processing. While prior work largely focuses on algorithmic failure, this study investigates the cognitive ergonomics and socio-cognitive impact of algorithmic competence. We present and evaluate FORMS (Framework for Opinion and Rhetoric in Multi-agent Simulations), a low-latency architecture for spatially mediated human-machine dialogue, driven by distinct LLM-based personas and real-time concurrency resolution. To conduct a system test and evaluation of its psychological impact, we exposed an adolescent cohort (n=120) and an adult pilot group (n=25) to a live, moderated synthetic debate. Our findings reveal that exposure to highly competent multi-agent systems triggers "Cognitive Destabilization," fragmenting users' prior strategic consensus. Concurrently, we observe a "Regulatory Awakening" driven by the "Normality Paradox": fluid human-machine interactions inherently increase the baseline demand for external regulation. Furthermore, our pilot study suggests the presence of a "Truthfulness Paradox": despite understanding the risks of generative AI, participants in the adult cohort rated the synthetic debate as significantly more sincere than equivalent human discourse (Cohen's d=2.04). Supported by robust statistical effect sizes, this paper contributes the FORMS architecture and a replicable evaluation protocol, illustrating how high-fidelity conversational systems can reshape human information processing.

items.title: Sistem Pendukung Keputusan Aset TI Berbasis LLM dengan Guardrail Domain
items.abstract: Manajemen aset Teknologi Informasi (TI) memerlukan keputusan yang dapat dipertanggungjawabkan berdasarkan data aset, riwayat pemeliharaan, kebutuhan pengguna, dan data monitoring. Penelitian ini mengusulkan sistem pendukung keputusan aset TI yang mengintegrasikan large language model, aturan guardrail domain, dan verifikasi human-in-the-loop. Sistem dikembangkan dengan pendekatan design science dan dievaluasi menggunakan 26 kasus uji yang mencakup aset dengan dan tanpa data monitoring, 78 eksekusi Artificial Intelligence (AI) berulang, pengujian teknis, serta penilaian ahli domain. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa fungsi AI menghasilkan keluaran terstruktur yang valid pada seluruh kasus dan relatif stabil pada eksekusi berulang. Representasi konteks Token-Oriented Object Notation (TOON) menurunkan rata-rata token sebesar 42,0% dibanding JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) mentah. Evaluasi ahli menunjukkan kesepakatan penuh pada 14 dari 15 kombinasi fitur-aspek, sedangkan satu kombinasi pada health aset tanpa data monitoring dan keakuratan klaim menunjukkan kesepakatan sebagian akibat perbedaan interpretasi temporal. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa dukungan keputusan berbasis Large Language Model (LLM) dengan guardrail domain dapat meningkatkan kejelasan dan kegunaan operasional rekomendasi aset TI.

items.title: Smart Home Automation and Security: Emerging Technologies, Cyber Security, and Future Innovations
items.abstract: Smart home automation and security have emerged as significant components of modern residential living due to rapid technological advancement and increasing digital connectivity. The integration of intelligent devices, communication networks, sensors, and automated control systems has transformed conventional homes into smart environments capable of improving convenience, energy efficiency, comfort, and safety. Smart home technology enables users to monitor and control household activities remotely through internet-enabled platforms and mobile applications. At the same time, modern security mechanisms provide real-time surveillance, automated alerts, controlled access, and threat detection capabilities. The concept of smart homes is closely connected with the Internet of Things (IoT), where interconnected devices communicate continuously to optimize home operations. Smart sensors, intelligent monitoring systems, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and machine learning collectively contribute to developing adaptive and responsive living spaces. These technologies provide improved management of lighting, temperature, energy consumption, appliance control, and security infrastructure. However, the widespread adoption of smart home systems also introduces challenges associated with cybersecurity, privacy protection, data security, and system reliability. Unauthorized access, cyberattacks, and data misuse have become major concerns requiring robust protective mechanisms.

items.title: Smart Oral Disintegrating Tablets: Integration of 3D Printing, AI, and Personalized Drug Delivery
items.abstract: Oral disintegrating tablets (ODTs) are easy and patient-friendly dosage forms that quickly dissolve in the mouth. They are especially useful for dysphagic, elderly, and pediatric patients. Conventional ODTs, on the other hand, are typically produced as standardized dosage forms and may have drawbacks with regard to dose flexibility, tablet design, drug loading, mechanical strength, and unique drug-release characteristics. Artificial intelligence (AI) and three-dimensional (3D) printing have opened up novel avenues for the creation of smart ODTs with digitally controlled and patient-focused features. While AI and machine learning (ML) can support formulation optimization, prediction of critical quality attributes, printability assessment, and selection of appropriate manufacturing parameters, 3D printing allows for customization of tablet geometry, internal structure, drug loading, porosity, and drug-release behavior. The creation of personalized ODTs with programmable release profiles, numerous drug combinations, on-demand manufacturing capabilities, and customizable doses may be made easier by the integration of AI/ML with 3D printing. Pediatric, elderly, dysphagic, and polypharmacy populations may find these systems especially helpful. Despite all these possible benefits, issues like restricted drug loading, mechanical strength, moisture sensitivity, taste masking, data quality, model validation, manufacturing reproducibility, scalability, cost, regulatory requirements, and patient-data security continue to be significant factors. Thus, smart ODTs is an emerging strategy for patient-centered, technologically enabled, and customized oral medication delivery. To incorporate these systems into standard pharmaceutical practice, more study, experimental validation, regulatory development, and digital technology integration is needed

items.title: Spectra Human-Centered Learning Framework: A Socio-Technical Architecture for AI-Supported Higher Education
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can produce persuasive university work without revealing who performed or checked the reasoning behind it. This conceptual article develops an AI-specific elaboration of the previously disseminated Spectra Human-Centered Learning Framework. Its three foundational conditions, six pedagogical phases and five original propositions are retained, not presented as new inventions. A purposive, critical synthesis distinguishes the functions of the pedagogical cycle and examines how AI assistance, intellectual responsibility, institutional safeguards and contextual constraints may intersect with them. The resulting architecture connects real-world input, conceptual framing, engagement, production, assessment and reflective transfer. The inherited propositions remain verbatim; task-level interpretations, candidate indicators and conditions that might challenge them are added for future research. Augmentation, dependency and substitution describe provisional distributions of work between learners and systems, not validated learner types. A targeted comparison with adjacent frameworks identifies overlaps and the specific scope of this elaboration without claiming global novelty or superiority. No student data were collected, no intervention was implemented and no systematic literature search was conducted. Whether the configuration supports independently defensible learning, accessible assessment and transfer across contexts remains an empirical question.

items.abstract: Using stepwise probe as an external reference or Chain-of-Thought (CoT) to evaluate visual-language model (VLM) analysis ability is common, but the faithfulness of PASS/FAIL verdicts in VLM produced by explicit CoT and independent SRFE probe needs further work to figure out. Prior works on CoT faithfulness are mainly about large language model (LLM) and internal interpretability signals, with limited VLM, Vision Prompt Distillation (VPD), structured verdict settings and behavioral probes. This paper focuses on evaluating Stepwise Reasoning Faithfulness Evaluation (SRFE), a five-step protocol (object->color->size->relation->composition) with prompt-defined order, and CoT faithfulness after distillation, trying to align them using probe Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to reduce two different methods to a single faithfulness evaluating method. To get features of SRFE, the paper compares the independent and conditional probe version and find weak chain effect in model then order ablation experiment find SRFE is order invariance. After VPD distillation on Qwen2-VL, teacher and student have a high agreement (97.6% stepwise, 88% exact bits), supporting SRFE probe is procedure faithfulness but not internal reasoning faithfulness. To find Chain-of-thought procedure faithfulness, the paper uses VLM to generate explicit CoT then separate the answer and compare each one under SRFE to get the similarity, finds that baseline CoT-SRFE probe partial misalignment. To improve alignment, SRFE probe supervised SFT on CoT is implemented, but finds a trade-off between independent probe agreement, chain consistency, and say-do &do-say.

items.title: Standardization in Healthcare Environments: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Background Healthcare systems are complex environments, and standardization is often viewed as a strategy to streamline complexity, reduce variability, improve patient safety, and enhance operational efficiency. While standardization has proven effective in industries such as aviation, nuclear plants, and manufacturing, its applicability in healthcare for its intended outcomes remains fundamentally contested . Additionally, current literature lacks a consistent definition or taxonomy of standardization in healthcare facility design. This creates conceptual ambiguity in both research and practice. Objective The aim of the scoping review is to develop a comprehensive understanding of the role of standardization in the healthcare-built environment, specifically focusing on inpatient settings, by examining how it has been studied and applied across healthcare settings. Method This review systematically searched peer-reviewed literature using the PRISMA-Scr structured framework to identify studies examining standardization in the healthcare-built environment. The review examined five databases using the Population, Concept, and Context framework, which guided keyword selection. Results The review included 28 articles and analyzed the aspects of standardization that have been studied, the rationale for its application, the implementation approach, and reported positive and negative outcomes across inpatient settings. Conclusions The findings suggest that the approach of standardization remains theoretical and conceptual, with very few studies empirically evaluating its outcomes. The existing literature suggests that standardization can reduce cognitive workload, improve workflow efficiency, and enhance safety when aligned with clinical processes and organizational culture. However, its implementation is challenged by the complexity and variability of healthcare delivery practices, resistance related to clinical autonomy, and limited integration across systems.

items.title: Statistical Process Control for Technical Cleanliness in Automotive Die-Casting: A Data-Driven Framework for Particle Contamination Monitoring and Reduction
items.abstract: This study proposes and validates a data-driven statistical process control (SPC) framework for monitoring and reducing particle contamination in automotive aluminium die-casting, addressing a documented gap in the structured application of inferential statistics to technical cleanliness management in automotive SMEs. An action research strategy based on DMAIC and CRISP-DM was conducted over eleven months in an automotive die-casting SME. The study encompassed a VDA 19.1/19.2-aligned audit, descriptive analysis of 64 pre-intervention samples, negative binomial regression with Wald hypothesis testing, Individual Moving Range (I-MR) control charts for before-and-after comparison, and microscopic characterisation of out-of-specification particles using Microsoft Excel, Minitab, and RStudio. The negative binomial model consistently outperformed Poisson regression across all granulometric classes (ΔAIC up to 2958.77). Mould cavity, injection machine condition, and injection operator were the dominant contamination predictors. Statistically significant variability reductions were achieved for total particles in the 150–400 µm range and for metallic particles in the 150–200 µm and 200–400 µm classes; the metallic 200–400 µm class also showed a significant mean reduction. Particles exceeding 400 µm remained dominated by sporadic special-cause events. The study is restricted to one component and site; the post-intervention sample (n = 17) limits statistical power, and extension to additional components, processes, and larger datasets is recommended. The reported findings should accordingly be read as case-study evidence rather than as generalisable, definitive conclusions. The framework offers a replicable, cost-effective approach to data-driven quality management for automotive SMEs, aligned with Industry 5.0 human-centric manufacturing principles. This paper bridges a literature gap by integrating negative binomial regression, Wald testing, and I-MR control charts into a unified SPC framework for technical cleanliness in automotive die-casting, connecting quality intelligence with the transversalities of artificial intelligence, innovation, and sustainability. The methodology itself relies on classical inferential statistics and SPC rather than on artificial intelligence algorithms; its Industry 5.0 relevance lies in providing the structured, human-centric, data-driven decision-making foundation on which future AI-assisted particle classification and real-time monitoring can be built.

items.title: Supportive AI in Image-Based Ophthalmology Evidence, Limitations, and Governance for Latin America
items.abstract: Within the selected corpus, there are image-based ophthalmology trials and artificial intelligence validations for bounded tasks. Fundus photography and optical coherence tomography allow detection, classification, and referral tasks to be delimited; however, algorithmic performance alone does not equate to clinical benefit, gap closure, or safe implementation. The most mature evidence concentrates on diabetic-retinopathy screening. A specific system received FDA De Novo authorization and, in its pivotal trial, reported 87.2% sensitivity and 90.7% specificity for detecting more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy in a defined population and indication. Those figures do not transfer to other tools or to Latin America. In retina and OCT, studies and reviews support classification and referral tasks, but validation depends on equipment, capture protocols, prevalence, and reference standard. In glaucoma, an SD-OCT meta-analysis reported a pooled sensitivity of 0.91 and specificity of 0.90, along with heterogeneity that limits any reading of universal readiness. The direct regional evidence identified includes two Mexican evaluations of AI-human support or comparison: a randomized reader experiment for diabetic-retinopathy images and an evaluation of 435 patients in tertiary care for glaucoma and retinal disease. Both works report performance in Mexican settings, not clinical outcomes, routine implementation, or validity for all of Latin America. A Brazilian economic model evaluated teleophthalmology without AI and contributes system context, not algorithmic effectiveness. For Latin American clinical teams, the current responsible use is support for screening, reading, prioritization, and referral within a governed care pathway. It is not yet possible to promise autonomous comprehensive ocular diagnosis, outcome benefit, reduction of inequities, or generalization across cameras, populations, and systems. The responsible agenda begins with retrospective feasibility, image governance, definition of the human response, and subgroup evaluation. Only after clinical and institutional approval would it be appropriate to design a silent prospective evaluation.

items.title: Synthetic Dermatology: Applications for Clinical Practice, Re-search, and Education
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning into medicine has launched a transformative epoch in dermatology, a specialty traditionally anchored in visual pattern recognition. While early machine learning research focused primarily on binary diagnostic classification, contemporary advancements have given rise to the para-digm of Synthetic Dermatology. This paradigm uses deep generative models such as Gen-erative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) together with personalized digital avatars, clinical large language models (LLMs), and multimodal tensor decompositions to synthesize complex clinical and histopathological images, gen-erate structured patient vignettes, and model real-world clinical trajectories. Herein, we review the state-of-the-art applications of synthetic technologies across three fundamental domains: clinical practice, dermatological research, and medical education, with a focus on personalizing dermatological care. By bridging the current clinical realities of hu-man-AI collaboration with a visionary perspective of the next decades, we outline how synthetic methodologies can mitigate data scarcity, address ethnic disparities in algo-rithmic diagnostics, optimize therapeutic regimens via cutaneous digital twins, and rede-fine student curricula. Finally, we critically appraise the technical, ethical, and regulatory hurdles that must be resolved to ensure the safe, equitable, and responsible translation of synthetic dermatology to patients.

items.title: Task Prioritization Under Varying Automation Reliability and Task Load in Multitasking Environments
items.abstract: Automation can improve efficiency in multitasking environments, but its benefits depend on system reliability and cognitive demands. This study examined the effects of automation reliability and task load on performance under task prioritization in a simulated multitasking environment. Twenty-six participants completed MATB-II tasks under four conditions varying in automation reliability (reliable vs. unreliable) and task load (low vs. high). Task performance and subjective workload were assessed across all conditions. Performance was highest under reliable, low-load conditions and declined with reduced automation reliability and increased task load across most tasks. Subjective workload increased under reduced automation reliability, whereas the effect of task load was not statistically significant. Notably, instructing participants to prioritize the tracking task did not result in preferential preservation of tracking task performance under reduced automation reliability and high task load conditions. These findings highlight the importance of reliable automation for supporting operator performance under high workload.

items.title: Testicular ergonomics: whole-body vibration, mechanotransduction, and male reproductive health in heavy machinery operators
items.abstract: Whole-body vibration (WBV) is a common occupational exposure among heavy machinery operators and has traditionally been investigated in relation to musculoskeletal, spinal, and neurological disorders. However, its potential impact on male reproductive health remains insufficiently characterized. This narrative review critically evaluates current occupational, experimental, and mechanobiological evidence concerning the potential association between chronic WBV exposure and male reproductive dysfunction. Particular attention is given to mechanotransduction and its potential interaction with oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, microvascular alterations, blood-testis barrier disruption, inflammation, endocrine alterations, and impaired spermatogenesis. Available evidence suggests biological plausibility but remains heterogeneous and insufficient to establish a causal relationship between occupational WBV and male infertility. We introduce the concept of Testicular Ergonomics as a hypothesis-generating framework for integrating male reproductive health into occupational vibration research and prevention. This framework emphasizes improved vibration exposure assessment, engineering and administrative controls, and standardized reproductive-health evaluation while accounting for relevant occupational and lifestyle confounders. Future prospective human and mechanistic studies integrating standardized WBV measurements with reproductive and molecular outcomes are required to determine whether chronic occupational vibration represents an independent risk to male reproductive health and to inform evidence-based preventive strategies.

items.title: The Accelerated Threat Landscape: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Scale and Complexity of Cybersecurity Threats: A Case Study
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the cyber domain has altered the conditions of cybersecurity as it has not only created unparalleled defensive potential but also increased risks to offensives. This paper explores how AI is affecting the magnitude and sophistication of cybersecurity threats, and how AI-based attack techniques are disruptive to current security models and increase the susceptibility of organizational IT systems. Using a qualitative case study, the data was gathered through cybersecurity professionals, artificial intelligence developers, and reported cyber-attacks to examine new attack vectors, such as deep fakes, automated malware, adversarial machine learning, and AI-powered social engineering. It was found that AI-enabled attacks are performed at machine speed, which enables threat actors to carry out highly coordinated, adaptable, and large-scale attacks that a conventional defense system could not detect or halt. At the same time, AI-based defensive solutions, including predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and automated response engines, exhibit the possibilities of threat mitigation before they actually happen though they are not actively used in the majority of organizations. The paper has emphasized the dual aspect of AI in cybersecurity and the urgent need by organizations to embrace AI-enhanced defenses and fortify governance structures and invest in workforce training to combat the increasing magnitude and complexity of threats. This study could be used by the policymakers, security professionals, and organizations to shape their strategies to cope with the new threat environment enforced by AI by defining major trends and gaps and providing practical recommendations.

items.title: The cost of ensembling: Is it always worth combining global retail forecasting models?
items.abstract: Given the continuous increase in dataset sizes and the complexity of forecasting models, the trade-off between forecast accuracy and computational cost is emerging as an extremely relevant topic, especially in the context of ensemble learning for time series forecasting. To assess it, we evaluated ten base models and eight ensemble configurations across two large-scale retail datasets, considering both point and probabilistic accuracy under varying retraining frequencies. We showed that ensembles consistently improve forecasting performance, particularly in probabilistic settings. However, these gains come at a substantial computational cost, especially for larger, accuracy-driven ensembles. We found that reducing retraining frequency significantly lowers costs, with minimal impact on accuracy, particularly for point forecasts. Moreover, efficiency-driven ensembles offer a strong balance, achieving competitive accuracy with considerably lower costs compared to accuracy-optimized combinations. Most importantly, small ensembles of two or three models are often sufficient to achieve near-optimal results. These findings provide practical guidelines for deploying scalable and cost-efficient forecasting systems, supporting the broader goals of sustainable artificial intelligence in forecasting.

items.title: THE DIGITAL MODE OF PRODUCTION AND THE TRANSFORMATION OF HIGHER EDUCATION IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between the digital mode of production and the transformation of the higher education model, using the Ho Chi Minh University of Banking as an empirical case study. Based on a political economy and educational governance framework, the research demonstrates that big data and artificial intelligence are restructuring the division of labor, thereby requiring higher education institutions to shift from a closed knowledge-transmission model toward an open, co-creative digital university ecosystem. In the case of HUB, the study identifies two key pillars of transformation: the restructuring of interdisciplinary digital-oriented curricula and data-driven training governance associated with a tripartite collaboration model. The findings provide significant scientific foundations for policy formulation and contribute to the development of high-quality human resources in the digital era.

items.title: The Effects of Correlated Color Temperature on Risky Decision-Making in Fatigued Individuals: An Event-Related Potential Study
items.abstract: Objective This study investigated the effects of correlated color temperature (CCT) on risky decision-making in fatigued individuals and the potential neural mechanisms underlying these effects. Background Underground facilities (UGFs) are increasingly utilized as military shelters, but the environmental stressors within them can easily lead to mental fatigue among commanders. The blue component within polychromatic white light, as indexed by CCT, has been shown to enhance alertness and cognition through non-visual pathways mediated by intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs). However, it remains unclear whether CCT can benefit risky decision-making in fatigued individuals during the day. Method We examined the effects of varying CCTs (4000 K, 6500 K, 8500 K, 12,000 K) on fatigued individuals using a within-subjects design ( N = 21) and assessed subjective alertness and mood, behavioral performance in attention and risky decision-making, and event-related potentials (ERP), including feedback-related negativity (FRN) and the P300 component. Results The results showed that 12,000 K led to more favorable decisions, reflected by a lower risk ratio, more cash-outs, and higher revenue. ERP analyses revealed larger FRN and P300 amplitudes under 12,000 K, indicating that higher CCT enhanced cognitive control and promoted more conservative decision-making, enabling beneficial feedback-based decisions even under fatigue. Conclusion Blue-enriched white light improves alertness, mood, and decision-making in fatigued individuals, promoting gain-maximizing and risk-minimizing decisions. Application The current findings demonstrate that CCT may serve as a key parameter for light-based interventions aimed at alleviating fatigue in risky decision-making in UGFs.

items.title: The elephants in the room
items.abstract: This chapter focuses on the two most seismic impacts on education within the last decade – the COVID-19 pandemic with its resultant social distancing and lockdowns and the recent emergence of ‘Generative Artificial Intelligence’. The COVID-19 pandemic changed the way in which online learning was used and impacted the experiences of many years’ worth of students’ education, social interactions, and peer-group structures. Similarly, generative AI is already changing the way in which students find information, undertake academic work, and even interact with each other and the world around them. This chapter suggests ways in which these factors have impacted (and continue to impact) self-regulated learning and the transition to university. This chapter provides some suggestions as to how the online learning space and generative AI can be used to enhance student learning and the development of self-regulatory skills.

items.title: The Functional Requirements of Person‐Centred Fundamental Care: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Against a Depleted Baseline
items.abstract: AIM: To propose provisional, theory-informed questions for evaluating whether artificial intelligence and robotic deployments support person-centred fundamental care when current practice is depleted. DESIGN: Discursive theoretical paper. METHODS: Purposive conceptual synthesis of fundamental care scholarship, selected behavioural and developmental theories, vulnerability scholarship, and illustrative technology evidence. RESULTS: Three lenses generate provisional questions about patient-specific meaning, connections among care activities over time, and the conditions sustaining responsive care. A separate ethical argument holds that delegating activities does not discharge professional or institutional obligations to patients. Applications to adaptive monitoring, social interaction, generative dialogue, and physical-task automation distinguish what the technology can do, how care work changes, and the effects on care. Hypothetical variations distinguish failures of interpretation, follow-through, and supporting conditions and identify grounds for favourable judgements. CONCLUSION: Improvement over current practice does not establish adequate person-centred fundamental care. Replacing an activity does not establish replacement of the care relationship. The questions require participatory refinement and empirical testing. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Nurses and leaders can use the questions to identify changes in care and work and deficits that remain, including when an imperfect deployment offers a justified improvement over feasible alternatives. IMPACT: The questions address inadequate care as an evaluation benchmark and offer patients, nurses, and decision-makers a way to evaluate technology deployment and service redesign. REPORTING METHOD: Discursive theoretical analysis; no applicable reporting checklist. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting.

items.title: The Governance of AI in Education: Developing Ethical Policy Frameworks for Adaptive Learning Technologies
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has transformed adaptive learning by personalizing instruction, automating assessments, and enhancing student engagement. However, the ethical challenges of AI governance, including algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, transparency gaps, and accountability issues, necessitate a structured regulatory framework. This study develops the Ethical AI Governance Framework for Adaptive Learning (EAGFAL) to address governance gaps and ensure fair, transparent, and responsible AI adoption in education. Using secondary data analysis and comparative case studies, the study examines global AI governance models, regulatory best practices, and ethical risks in AIdriven education. Findings highlight that inconsistent regulatory approaches contribute to disparities in AI deployment, with some regions favoring market-driven AI policies, while others enforce strict legal oversight. The study recommends bias mitigation strategies, explainable AI mechanisms, and robust data governance policies to ensure AI-driven education remains inclusive, ethical, and student-centered. EAGFAL offers practical policy insights for governments, educators, and AI developers, advocating for cross-sector collaboration to align AI innovation with ethical responsibility. Future research should explore long-term impacts, scalability, and evolving governance structures for ethical AI integration in education.

items.title: The impact of AI chatbot service quality on consumer purchase intention: the cognitive and affective mediating mechanisms
items.abstract: Introduction The increasing prevalence of artificial intelligence chatbots in e-commerce raises questions about how the service quality dimensions of AI chatbots may influence consumer purchase intentions. Drawing on Expectation-Confirmation Theory, the Information Systems Success Model, and the Technology Acceptance Model, this study proposes a conceptual framework to examine these relationships. Methods Survey data were collected from 493 Chinese consumers with prior experience using AI chatbots. The study examined perceived personalization, social presence, information quality, and human-AI service continuity as possible antecedents of purchase intention. Perceived usefulness and satisfaction were treated as mediating variables. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used for the analysis with 5,000 bootstrapped resamples. Results Perceived personalization, social presence, information quality, and human-AI service continuity were associated with perceived usefulness. Additionally, perceived personalization, information quality, and human-AI service continuity were positively associated with satisfaction. Conversely, social presence did not show a significant direct effect on satisfaction. Both perceived usefulness and satisfaction are linked to purchase intention, with satisfaction having a stronger direct connection. The mediation analysis revealed that perceived usefulness and satisfaction mediate the relationship between AI chatbot service quality and purchase intention. The only exception was the indirect effect of social presence through satisfaction, which was not statistically significant. Discussion This study seeks to contribute to understanding how the service quality of AI chatbots influences consumers’ purchase intentions through perceived usefulness and satisfaction. The results indicate that information quality is the most significant among the service quality dimensions in AI-mediated interactions. The lack of a significant direct impact of social presence on satisfaction suggests that, in utilitarian-oriented e-commerce environments, consumers are more likely to prioritize functional service features over social–emotional factors when assessing AI chatbot services. These findings may inform e-commerce practitioners seeking to improve AI-driven customer service by emphasizing information accuracy and completeness, enhancing personalization, and fostering seamless human-AI service continuity to drive purchase conversions.

items.title: The impact of AI on the advertising industry in Spain: uncertainty and threats according to professionals in the sector
items.abstract: This exploratory study aims to analyse the perceptions of professionals in the field of marketing and advertising regarding the risks and threats associated with the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the sector. Through a survey with a sample of 373 marketing, advertising, and branded content professionals in Spain, the concerns of participants were uncovered regarding the quality of AI-generated content, the potential loss of creativity and originality, the impact on job security, and the need for human oversight. While the participants appreciate the operational utility of AI, they also warn of its ethical, expressive, and strategic limitations. The findings reveal a perspective that is critical, although not technophobic, which calls for regulatory frameworks, specialised training, and responsible use. In regards to the practical implications, this study highlights the tension that accompanies automation in the creative field and underscores the importance of ethical, balanced, and human-focused use of such technology, which is the prerequisite for a responsible transition toward the use of AI in the advertising industry. Given the context, it is imperative to understand how the transformation of the industry due to the introduction of these technologies is interpreted by the professionals who experience them firsthand. This study is one of the first to evaluate the level of acceptance of AI tools among professionals in the advertising industry in Spain.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Service Quality and Operational Efficiency in Healthcare: An Empirical Analysis
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a game changer in the healthcare industry, with profound effects on operational effectiveness and service quality. This empirical study examines how AI adoption affects the provision of healthcare services, concentrating on two main aspects: improving operational efficiency (resource allocation, patient waiting times, administrative workflows, and cost reduction) and improving service quality (diagnostic accuracy, patient satisfaction, and care personalization). The study used a standardized survey instrument that was given to [N] administrators and healthcare workers from various healthcare facilities, utilizing a quantitative research approach. To find statistically significant correlations between AI adoption levels and key performance measures, data were analyzed using multiple regression, correlation analysis, and descriptive statistics.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Technology Applications on the Employment Structure of the Labor Force
items.abstract: Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have occurred alongside digitization, big data, and computing power and have significantly impacted how the global labor market works. This paper examines the effects of AI applications on the labor market and the structure of the workforce. The main method of research is literature review; academic articles on the implementation of AI and its effects on the workforce are reviewed and analyzed to understand skill-biased and task-biased technological changes along with displacement, reinforcement, and productivity effects of AI. This paper finds that AI contributes to increasing the demand for highly skilled workers who would be able to complement intelligent systems while reducing the demand for simple professions and jobs that can be automated. However, the overall impact on employment is weak so far due to the offset of job losses resulting from automation by the emergence of new job positions at more productive companies using AI.

items.title: The Implementation of STEM Approach on English Learning in Students Writing Activities at SMP Negeri 12 Gorontalo
items.abstract: The integration of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) into English language instruction has emerged as an innovative approach to support meaningful learning experiences and enhance students’ writing development. This study aimed to explore the implementation of STEM-based English writing instruction and examine its contribution to students’ engagement and writing development at SMP Negeri 12 Gorontalo. Employing a descriptive qualitative design, the study involved one English teacher and twenty-six eighth-grade students. Data were collected through classroom observations, semi-structured interviews, and documentation of students’ written products. The findings revealed that STEM was implemented through a series of interconnected learning activities, including direct observation, technology-assisted learning, collaborative project construction, descriptive writing tasks, revision activities, and reflective presentations. The integration of STEM elements facilitated students’ active participation throughout the learning process and promoted behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement. Furthermore, STEM-based activities supported students’ writing development by providing authentic learning experiences that enabled them to generate ideas, organize information, expand vocabulary use, and produce contextualized descriptive texts. The findings also indicated that project-based STEM activities fostered creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, which contributed positively to the quality of students’ written products. Although some students continued to experience difficulties related to grammar and language accuracy, most were able to communicate ideas effectively and produce writing that reflected their observation and project experiences. These findings suggest that STEM-based English writing instruction offers a meaningful pedagogical framework for enhancing student engagement and supporting writing development through contextual, collaborative, and project-oriented learning experiences.

The results indicate that OHS, Work Environment, and Employee Engagement simultaneously influence employee performance at PT. Waskita Karya (Persero) Tbk, with a significance level of 0.000 < α (0.05), meaning the null hypothesis (Ho) is rejected and the alternative hypothesis (Ha) is accepted. items.title: The Mediating Roles of Satisfaction and Perceived Intelligence In Chatgpt Adoption Among Research and Development Employees: An Extended Technology Acceptance Model
items.abstract: This study examines how employees in corporate research and development (R&D) units form the intention to use ChatGPT at work, a population that remains underexplored compared with the student samples dominating prior research. Building on an extended Technology Acceptance Model, the study tests whether perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and awareness shape behavioural intention to use, with satisfaction and perceived intelligence positioned as dual mediators. Data from 190 R&D employees in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia, obtained through purposive sampling, were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). All eight hypothesised direct paths were supported: ease of use and usefulness strengthen satisfaction, awareness builds perceived intelligence, and all five predictors raise behavioural intention, with perceived usefulness as the dominant driver. Perceived intelligence and satisfaction partially transmit the effects of awareness and usefulness, respectively. The findings direct organisations to anchor workplace artificial intelligence adoption strategies in demonstrated usefulness and structured awareness-building.

items.title: The Multidimensional Relationship Between Algorithmic Media Content Awareness and Artificial Intelligence Literacy: A Study on University Students
items.abstract: This study aims to examine the relationship between university students’ algorithmic content awareness and artificial intelligence literacy levels, and to reveal the interaction pattern between these two competency domains. As algorithmic systems increasingly shape how individuals access information, users’ ability to understand and critically evaluate these systems has become essential. In this context, the study highlights the role of cognitive awareness beyond mere technological exposure. The study was conducted using a correlational survey design, a quantitative research method. Data were collected from 534 students enrolled at Selçuk University through a structured questionnaire. The dataset was filtered based on missing data, straight-lining responses (longstring bias), and inconsistent response patterns in reverse-coded items. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), mediation analysis, and canonical correlation analysis were employed in the data analysis process. The findings indicate a positive and moderate significant relationship between algorithmic awareness and artificial intelligence literacy (r = .464, p < .001). Structural model results show that algorithmic awareness significantly predicts artificial intelligence literacy (β = .47, p < .001). Canonical correlation analysis revealed a moderate level of shared variance between the two variable sets (Rc = .473; Rc² = .224). However, social media usage time did not have a significant indirect effect on artificial intelligence literacy through algorithmic awareness (ab = .025, p = .244). The results suggest that technological exposure alone is not sufficient; rather, artificial intelligence literacy develops through cognitive processes associated with critical awareness of algorithmic systems.

items.title: The Psychological Mechanisms and Social Implications of Over-Trust in AI Chat-Based on GPT-4 Persuasion Experiments
items.abstract: As large language models have been increasingly applied to daily life in information seeking and decision-making, public trust in AI output has greatly improved. This brings about the worry that human critical thinking could become impaired. Using Salvi et al.'s GPT-4 conversational persuasion experiment as a start, this paper adopts a literature review method and relies on the theory of automation bias as well as cognitive laziness. This paper uses literature review as the way of research and utilizes the theories such as automation bias and cognitive laziness, etc., to explore the psychological mechanism behind the power of AI's ability to persuade others, and how it affects different people's minds. Findings indicate that the notable persuasiveness of AI stems primarily from two interrelated psychological mechanisms: cognitive laziness, which inclines individuals to forgo independent verification, and algorithm worship, which inclines individuals to delegate cognitive authority to AI systems. Both mechanisms manifest across adolescent and adult populations and may contribute to the erosion of critical thinking through prolonged AI use. The national, corporate, educational, individual levels response strategies are put forward in this paper, and the future research directions including cross-cultural comparison studies, longitudinal follow-up researches and individual-difference study plans are given out.

items.title: The Relationship Between Artificial Intelligence Literacy and Artificial Intelligence Anxiety: The Case of Medical School Resident Physicians
items.abstract: Aim: To examine the relationship between resident physicians' Artificial Intelligence literacy levels and their anxiety towards Artificial Intelligence, and to evaluate differences according to sociodemographic variables. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 296 resident physicians working at Necmettin Erbakan University Faculty of Medicine between January and February 2025. Data were collected via an online survey comprising a sociodemographic information form and questions regarding attitudes, experiences of AI, the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale, and the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale. The data were analysed using the SPSS 25.0 programme, with independent simple t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and Pearson's correlation analysis being employed. The significance level was set at p<0.05. Results: Scale scores were found to be significantly higher among those who spent more time online, those with experience with AI, and individuals interested in Artificial Intelligence. The Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale score was higher in women and in individuals who believed that artificial intelligence could replace them in the future. A significant negative correlation was found between the total Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale score and the usage and evaluation sub-dimension and the learning sub-dimension of the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale. Conclusion: This suggests that personal experiences and educational factors influence perceptions of artificial intelligence. Integrating Artificial Intelligence knowledge and applications into medical education may enhance physicians’ awareness and attitudes.

items.title: The relationship between self-determination theory–based L2 motivation and L2 achievement: A multilevel meta-analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Over the past decades, self-determination theory (SDT) has been widely applied in second language (L2) motivation research. The present study employed a multilevel meta-analysis to examine the direction and magnitude of the relationship between SDT-based L2 motivation and L2 achievement. We systematically searched ten English databases and pooled the data using random-effects models. A total of 74 eligible studies involving 220 estimates were included in the analyses. The results showed that both intrinsic motivation ( r = .318, p < .001) and extrinsic motivation ( r = .166, p < .001) were significantly and positively correlated with L2 achievement. Two autonomous dimensions of extrinsic motivation—integrated regulation ( r =. 248, p < .001) and identified regulation ( r = .190, p < .001)—were positively related with L2 achievement, whereas controlled dimensions—introjected regulation ( r = .006, p = .866) and external regulation ( r = .010, p = .781)—were not. The aggregated associations between intrinsic/extrinsic motivation and L2 achievement were moderated by learning context and teaching mode. Theoretical and practical implications of this study are discussed.

items.title: The Role of Adaptive Learning Technologies in Personalized Education
items.abstract: As educational systems strive to move beyond "one-size-fits-all" pedagogical models, Adaptive Learning Technologies (ALTs) powered by Artificial Intelligence (AI) have emerged as a critical solution for personalization. This paper presents a systematic literature review examining the efficacy of ALTs in enhancing learner engagement, academic performance, and equity. Analyzing peer-reviewed studies published between 2019 and 2025, the review focuses on the transition from rule-based systems to advanced Machine Learning (ML) algorithms, specifically contrasting Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) with Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) and Transformer-based models. Key findings indicate that ALTs yield a significant positive effect on cognitive learning outcomes and bolster student motivation (Chaudhry et al., 2025; Martinez & Anderson, 2024). However, the study identifies critical barriers, including the "cold start" problem, algorithmic bias in minority representations, and the "Black Box" opacity of neural networks (Baker & Hawn, 2021; Heaven, 2024). The paper concludes that while ALTs are potent tools for democratization, their sustainable success is contingent upon the integration of Explainable AI (XAI) frameworks and robust fairness-aware algorithms (Liu et al., 2024).
